batch: NWE (the v5 re-run order, interactive dispatch, 2026-10-25)

runs.name: NorthWestern Energy Group, Inc.; Nasdaq NWE, Delaware, 10-K filer; regulated electric and gas utility in Montana, South Dakota and Nebraska; all-stock merger of equals with Black Hills signed 2025-08-18, awaiting the Montana order
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: Next name owed in `Screens/_daily/_v5_rerun_order.txt` (NI, ahead of it, has an unfolded run of 2026-10-23 killed after Q7 and is a resume, not a dispatch); interactive dispatch under the canonical brief, lock held by the main session; the brief's one departure is the repository path after the move of 2026-10-25 (C:\Projects\BRK). Price **$77.59** (2026-10-23, aggregator, flagged) x **61,517,850 shares** (one class, 10-Q cover `0001993004-26-000050`) = cap **$4,773M**; sovereign **5.33%** (Treasury 30-year, 2026-10-23). Q1 IN (rate base $5.57B at end-2025, Montana electric $3.68B; allowed ROE 9.65% electric and 9.60% gas on a 47.84% equity layer; every Montana case of the decade settled below the ask, the 2024 order with a $30.9M Yellowstone County disallowance; 10-K `0001993004-26-000006`). Q2 IN on the regulated-return exception, the electric segment deciding at 85.6% of five-year operating profit; wildfire liability limited by statute in both states; 55% of Colstrip Units 3 and 4 taken for $0. Q3 against; Q4 accounts IN, weighing against; Q5 integrity IN, ability against (the allowed return not earned in any year since 2019, the gap 3.3 points in 2025); Q6 against on both parts (dividends of $742M over five years paid from borrowings and issued shares against $162M of owner cash after maintenance; the sale for stock at no premium with awards accelerated). Q7 OUT on the floor: owner cash after the filer's own maintenance guess $32.4M a year (2021 to 2025; after depreciation $144.0M; after all spending negative); range the no-growth case alone, **$9.87 a share equity-only (central, regulated utility)**, the depreciation variant $43.90 beside, all-equity not positive; price above the top of every case; fair price **$5.26 equity-only** ($23.40 depreciation variant; all-equity negative). The utility debt credit ($103.8M a year, cap 52.0%) enters only the growth illustration, where growth destroys value. The merger beside on the combined averages: 0.98 BKH a share, $77.82 as if closed, combined depreciation-basis yield 4.1%, changes nothing. Peers (earned ROE, decade means, own filings): NWE 8.5% falling to 6.3% in 2025, BKH 8.6%, AVA 7.6%, IDA 9.5%, ALE 7.4% (stopped filing after FY2024), MDU 9.8% not comparable before its spin-offs. Framework notes for the operator in the run file: the Whose-tax statutory rate against a utility whose flow-through benefits belong to customers (confessed departure, as-filed cash central); the all-stock STOP written for the acquirer only; specific (b) switching off the utility machinery; whether a regulated filer's maintenance figure is the guess the rows mean; a fair price under a signed all-stock deal. Dispatcher's check: check_framework PASS; the analyst's `check_ids.py` PASS re-run by the dispatcher; four pathspec commits, own paths only; lapse declared in the file: Q3 to Q6 in one commit. Contamination declared: root and `Screens/` listings showed file names, none opened. Position note filled at the fold: not held. Armed at the equity-only fair price; the run's own re-look line names the top of the computed range, $43.90, beside it.
runs.narr: A regulated utility that has not earned its allowed return since 2019 and pays its dividend from borrowings and issued shares, selling itself for Black Hills stock at no premium. Q1 and Q2 IN on the franchise, Q3 to Q6 against, OUT at Q7 on the floor: range $9.87 equity-only (depreciation variant $43.90) vs $77.59, fair $5.26 ($23.40). The run's framework notes on the utility tax convention and the all-stock STOP are owed a reading.
